purpose: Derive and independently benchmark the exact local result that every healthy active homogeneous timelike background of P0(X)+Z(X)Y with X>0, Y>0 and Z_X nonzero has one scalar characteristic speed below and one above the g-null speed, without promoting metric-cone superluminality to an unconditional causality violation.

source_or_paper_gate.rule: A theorem-only result may advance on primary papers plus independent exact analytic and numerical checks. Any later observational builder must separately bind a suitable real public source and response dataset before scoring.

theorem.action_slice: P=P0(X)+Z(X)Y on an aligned homogeneous timelike background
hypotheses: P0 and Z are C2 locally
the exact scalar kinetic matrix K and spatial-gradient matrix G are symmetric positive definite

definitions.characteristic_speeds: the two positive generalized eigenvalues c_s^2 of G v=c_s^2 K v

theorem.proof: Because K and G are positive definite, the generalized speeds are real and positive. The characteristic polynomial det(G-c^2 K) is positive at c^2=0, negative at c^2=1, and positive as c^2 tends to infinity. Therefore exactly one root lies in (0,1) and the other in (1,infinity).
theorem.conclusion: Every healthy active background in this architecture has c_-^2<1<c_+^2 relative to the g-null cone.
theorem.independence_from_P0: P0 changes the diagonal kinetic entry and the numerical speeds but cannot change det(K-G), so no choice of P0 removes straddling while X,Y,Z_X remain active.
escape_cases: a degenerate or non-positive K or G outside the theorem hypotheses
a different action architecture with additional derivative operators that change both K and G
